back: ρ = RA/L, where R is the resistance of a uniform sample of length L and cross-sectional area A; unit Ω m.
R ∝ L and R ∝ 1/A ∝ 1/d²: doubling the diameter quarters the resistance.

front: Stretching a wire to n times its length (constant volume)
back: Area falls by n, so the resistance rises by n².
Metals ~10⁻⁸ Ω m; alloys ~10⁻⁶ Ω m; semiconductors ~10⁻¹–10³ Ω m; insulators 10¹⁰ Ω m and above.
Metals: ρ rises (more lattice collisions). Semiconductors: ρ falls (more charge carriers).
Plot R against L: gradient = ρ/A, so ρ = gradient × A; a positive intercept is contact resistance.

front: Largest uncertainty in a resistivity experiment
back: The diameter: small and squared in A, so its percentage uncertainty is doubled.
